newsitem.title: BELGIUM: New EU aid rules to help shipping sector.
newsitem.headline: New EU aid rules to help shipping sector.

text.p: The European Commission adopted new rules for state aid in the maritime transport sector on Tuesday, saying urgent action was needed to stop the decline in European Union fleets.

The revised guidelines, aimed at encouraging the development of the bloc's shipping sector, will allow EU member states to exempt shipping from fiscal and social charges or to reimburse those charges.

"Action is urgently needed to prevent the further decline in the Union flagged fleet which brings with it loss of know-how and jobs in shipping and related on-shore activities," the EU executive said in a statement.

The new rules reflect the fact that the competitive difference between ships registered in the 15-nation EU and those operated especially under flags of convenience depends on fiscal costs such as corporate taxation and wage charges.
Today, roughly one third of the world fleet is owned by companies established in the EU but only some 12 percent is registered there.
Guidelines adopted in 1989 allowed member states to compensate shipowners for the cost gap between operations under a flag of convenience and those under an EU flag.
"However, the calculation method developed to determine the cost gap for different flags and different ship types has proven difficult to apply in practice," the Commission said.
"The revised guidelines...propose a more transparent method in that member states are allowed to exempt shipping from fiscal and social charges or to reimburse these charges."

Corporate tax relief may in certain limited circumstances be applied to earnings derived from all vessels operated by a company established in a member state for which it exercises "the strategic, commercial and safety management," it said.
The Commission also said the new guidelines take a "positive approach" to training aid.
